H1.title: Cumulative diff exceeds the review limit
H1.resolution: The owner explicitly authorized the large-diff path before implementation; signed history is not destructively rewritten solely to repartition the same independently reviewed code. Risk is mitigated by two independent critics plus locked Rust, zero-skip desktop, wheel, and full repository gates.

history.resolution: The owner explicitly authorized the large-diff path before implementation; signed history is not destructively rewritten solely to repartition the same independently reviewed code. Risk is mitigated by two independent critics plus locked Rust, zero-skip desktop, wheel, and full repository gates.

H2.title: Positive fixtures are not Windows-portable
H2.resolution: Rust and Python now keep paths as platform-neutral wire strings and apply one lexical POSIX/drive-qualified Windows grammar; shared positive fixtures exercise both styles on every host.

history.resolution: Rust and Python now keep paths as platform-neutral wire strings and apply one lexical POSIX/drive-qualified Windows grammar; shared positive fixtures exercise both styles on every host.

H3.title: Nested extension fields violate minor compatibility
H3.resolution: Only top-level extension keys require a namespace; nested payload keys retain ordinary JSON semantics, guarded by a shared mixed-case compatible-minor fixture.

history.resolution: Only top-level extension keys require a namespace; nested payload keys retain ordinary JSON semantics, guarded by a shared mixed-case compatible-minor fixture.

H4.title: Decoder causes retain the startup token
H4.resolution: UTF-8 and JSON decoder failures are converted outside exception handlers through payload-free sentinels; recursive exception-graph tests prove malformed canaries are absent.

history.resolution: UTF-8 and JSON decoder failures are converted outside exception handlers through payload-free sentinels; recursive exception-graph tests prove malformed canaries are absent.

H5.title: Sidecar reflects rather than verifies executable SHA
H5.resolution: The sidecar hashes current_exe before binding, compares the expected digest in fixed time, emits the computed digest, and rejects a one-nibble mismatch with no endpoint announcement.

history.resolution: The sidecar hashes current_exe before binding, compares the expected digest in fixed time, emits the computed digest, and rejects a one-nibble mismatch with no endpoint announcement.

M1.title: Executable-version validation diverges by language
M1.anchor: and all(character.isascii() and character.isprintable() for character in version)
M1.resolution: Python now matches Rust's visible ASCII executable-version grammar, with a shared negative fixture for embedded space.

M2.title: Invalid-token stderr guard checks the wrong canary
M2.resolution: The invalid-launch process regression now checks the exact invalid token sent to the sidecar as well as the original capability.
